clue.text: A doctor provided treatment, initially without purpose

parts.note: provided, as in 'provided that', means if

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word treatment

explanation.surface: A physician gives some therapy, but at first seems to have no clear aim.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat cut loose drifts aimlessly, so someone lacking direction or a goal is said to be at sea in this way.

clue.text: Sweltering in outskirts of Delhi in this?

definitions.text: Sweltering in outskirts of Delhi in this?

indicators.note: in tells us the word for sweltering sits between those edge letters
outskirts are the edges of a town, so the first and last letters of Delhi are used

parts.note: sweltering means very hot

explanation.surface: In the heat at the edge of an Indian city, this is what you might wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a light loincloth suited to sweltering Indian heat.
explanation.definitionFit: This loincloth worn by men in India is a cool garment for a hot climate.

clue.text: Idle characters gather round person in silly position?

indicators.note: round tells us the word for gather goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: to gather from evidence is to infer

indicators.note: characters means the letters of Idle are taken as loose characters and rearranged

explanation.surface: Lazy people cluster about someone in a ridiculous stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle' looks like the lazy folk of the surface; 'characters' marks its letters for rearranging. Silly mid-on and silly point are cricket fielding positions close to the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly fielding positions in cricket lie close to the wicket, so anyone placed there is one of the close-in team.

clue.text: Order from Italy union wants to check

parts.note: TU is the abbreviation for trade union
to scan something is to check it

explanation.surface: A trade union in Italy wants to keep a rule in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' is a classical architectural order, a style of column.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five classical styles of column, a simplified Doric, takes its name from a region of central Italy.

clue.text: Infantry occupy secure position for advance

parts.note: foot soldiers are the infantry, so foot can stand for it
to occupy a place is to hold it

explanation.surface: Foot soldiers take a strong position from which to push forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber's or army's firm base from which further progress can be made is literally a place to plant a foot.

clue.text: Device used by post-impressionists?

parts.note: read not as the art movement but as people who impress or stamp the post, marking letters to show postage is paid

explanation.surface: Asks what equipment artists such as Cezanne and Gauguin used.
explanation.walkthrough: Post-impressionism was an art movement; here the word is split as those who impress post.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine in a mailroom stamps envelopes to show postage paid, impressing a mark on the mail.

clue.text: Like a good monk, taking to Bede in translation

indicators.note: translation turns words into another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A model monk gets on with translating the Venerable Bede.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the anagram. Bede was an Anglo-Saxon monk and historian.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks take vows of obedience, so a good one does as he is told.

clue.text: Jute of top quality? Sounds rougher

indicators.note: Sounds tells us the answer is said like a word for rougher

parts.note: a rougher voice is a hoarser one

explanation.surface: Asks whether the finest jute fibre feels coarser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jute' is not the fibre but a member of the Germanic tribe. In non-rhotic British speech the homophone works.
explanation.definitionFit: With his brother Hengist, this legendary leader of the Jutes landed in Kent in the fifth century, so he was a Jute of high rank.

clue.text: Relaxed? Certainly, with Hawaiian garland on

indicators.note: on means placed on top, so in this down clue the garland comes first

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland
surely means certainly

explanation.surface: Feeling at ease? Of course, wearing a garland of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhurried and easy-going describes doing something at a slow, comfortable pace.

clue.text: Appropriate fact is once misconstrued

indicators.note: misconstrued means wrongly understood, so the letters of the preceding words are taken in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A suitable fact was once misinterpreted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective but is the verb meaning to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate property is to take it for oneself, as an authority seizing goods does.

clue.text: Track of a wading bird

definitions.meaning: a railway line or bar along which something runs
a marsh bird such as the water ... or corncrake

explanation.surface: Footprints left by a bird that wades.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail is both the steel bar trains run on and a family of secretive marsh birds.

clue.text: In which a churchwarden may stand out

definitions.text: In which a churchwarden may stand out

parts.words: In which a churchwarden may stand out
parts.note: a churchwarden is also a long-stemmed clay pipe for smoking, and here it is stored upright on a stand with other tobacco pipes

explanation.surface: A church official is conspicuous in some setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The parish officer is a red herring: a churchwarden is a clay pipe with a very long stem.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand or holder for tobacco pipes is where such a long clay pipe would be kept upright.

clue.text: Such endless air trouble for this early aviator

indicators.note: trouble, as a verb meaning to stir up, tells us to rearrange the letters
endless means the word Such loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Air turbulence of this kind bothered a pioneer of flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts Such to SUC; 'trouble' shuffles SUC with AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this figure flew on wings of wax and feathers made by Daedalus, long before any real flight.

clue.text: Boss of the establishment relying on good breeding

definitions.meaning: a raised knob or ornamental ..., as on a shield
a farm where horses are kept for breeding

explanation.surface: The head of a firm depends on a good pedigree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' suggests a manager; here it is a decorative knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a projecting knob like a shield boss, and also a farm for breeding horses.

clue.text: Paper shredder of great help

indicators.note: a shredder cuts paper into pieces, so the letters are torn up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A machine for shredding documents is a big help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper shredder' reads as one office machine; 'Paper' is the definition, a British national newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily ___ is a British national newspaper.

clue.text: Period, last century, of Einstein's development

indicators.note: development suggests the letters growing into a new shape, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A stage in the twentieth century when the great physicist's work progressed.
explanation.definitionFit: The final decade of a hundred years, such as 1990 to 1999, is named after its tens figure.

clue.text: Typewriter piece to be forbidden in the future, you say?

indicators.note: you say tells us the answer is how the phrase is pronounced

parts.words: to be forbidden in the future
parts.note: forbidden means taboo and in the future means later

explanation.surface: A typewriter part that is due to be banned, someone claims.
explanation.definitionFit: On a typewriter, the key and mechanism that jumps the carriage to set column stops is a component for lining up columns.

clue.text: Scholarly people among the elite, ratings-wise

indicators.note: among tells us the answer sits inside the run of letters in the elite, ratings-wise

explanation.surface: Learned folk rank high in the elite according to ratings.
explanation.definitionFit: Educated, well-read people interested in literature form an intellectual class.

clue.text: Concern for others, expressed as a Liberal platitude

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal in politics
a platitude is a trite, obvious statement, a truism

explanation.surface: Selflessness, a politician claims, is just a commonplace remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Selflessness means putting other people's welfare before one's own.

clue.text: Sounds like hounds or hunters, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a hound's deep howling cry is called baying
hunters are horses used in hunting, and reddish-brown horses are called by this colour

explanation.surface: A noise resembling that of dogs or men on the chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' looks like a homophone signal but is part of the definition: what hounds do.
explanation.definitionFit: Hounds give voice with a deep bark, and brown horses with black manes, often hunting mounts, share the name.

clue.text: A place to meet and drive \

parts.note: a venue is a place where people meet or an event is held

explanation.surface: Somewhere to get together and go for a spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' looks like a verb; it is a noun, a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a road, often a broad, tree-lined residential one.

clue.text: Brown coal left out to burn

indicators.note: out tells us the letter for left is removed from the coal

parts.note: lignite is soft brown coal

explanation.surface: Some brown coal was left outside to be set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: To set fire to something is to make it start burning.

clue.text: Is putting new metal in anvil

indicators.note: in tells us the new metal goes inside the word is

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, a metal

explanation.surface: A smith says new metal goes onto the anvil.
explanation.walkthrough: The smithy picture misleads: the anvil is the small bone of the middle ear.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny bone of the middle ear is named after the Latin for a blacksmith's anvil, which it resembles.

clue.text: As supercilious as Caroline?

definitions.meaning: belonging to the time of King Charles I, whose royalist supporters bore this name

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone is as haughty as a woman named Caroline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caroline' looks like a woman's name; it is the adjective for the reign of Charles (Latin Carolus).
explanation.definitionFit: The word means offhand and disdainful, and was also the name for royalist supporters of Charles I in the English Civil War.

clue.text: With sweetheart run

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E
to lope is to run with a long easy stride

explanation.surface: Run off together with a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: to run away secretly with a sweetheart to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers who run off secretly to marry without consent do exactly this.

clue.text: Brandy to spoil concentration at first

parts.note: to spoil something is to mar it

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of concentration

explanation.surface: Drinking spirits ruins your ability to focus right from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit distilled from the skins and pips left after grapes are pressed for wine is a kind of brandy.

clue.text: Estrangement from Natalie? No. I reform

indicators.note: reform means form again, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Natalie's partner says no to reconciling, refusing to change.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cut off emotionally from someone once close is a kind of separation or isolation.

clue.text: Whip. Conservative, is in hurry

indicators.note: in tells us the word is goes inside the word for hurry

parts.note: haste means hurry

explanation.surface: A party whip, a Tory, is in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' looks like the party official; it is the verb meaning to punish.
explanation.definitionFit: To whip someone is to punish them physically, to scold or beat.

clue.text: Apprentice does not begin to be a breadwinner

indicators.note: does not begin means the word for apprentice loses its opening letter

parts.note: an apprentice is a learner of a trade

explanation.surface: A trainee doesn't start out as the family's provider.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who brings in income, especially for a household, is the one who gets paid.
